item.title: 5.1.1. AWS Sign-in and Region
item.description:
5.1.1. AWS Sign-in and Region

Objective

Select the correct us-east-1 Region, verify AWS Console access, and create budget alerts for the lab.

Steps

  1. Sign in with an IAM user or a delegated account; do not share the root account across the team.
  2. Select United States (N. Virginia) — us-east-1 in the Region selector. Regional resources such as EC2, DynamoDB, Lambda, and API Gateway should be inspected in the same Region.

  1. Navigate to Billing and Cost Management → Budgets → Create budget. Select a Cost budget and enter the planned limit (the group’s earlier lab used USD 20/month).

item.title: 5.2.1. Create a VPC, Subnets, Routes, and IGW
item.description:
5.2.1. Create a VPC, Subnets, Routes, and IGW

Objective

Build a virtual network for the monitored EC2 instance, separating Internet-facing and internal resources.

AWS Console steps

  1. Go to VPC → Your VPCs → Create VPC. Choose an appropriate configuration. observed VPC CIDR 10.0.0.0/16.
  1. Create a public subnet (e.g., 10.0.0.0/20) and a private subnet (e.g., 10.0.128.0/20) in the appropriate Availability Zone.
  1. Create an Internet Gateway and attach it to the VPC.
  1. Create a public route table, add 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to the Internet Gateway, and associate it with the public subnet.
  1. A private subnet has no automatic Internet access. If outbound Internet access is required, design NAT appropriately and consider the cost before creating it.
  2. Review Network ACLs and Security Groups against the required traffic flows and deny unnecessary access.

Evidence to capture

  • VPC, CIDR ranges, and subnet list.
  • Route table and Internet Gateway association.
  • Security Group attached to EC2.

Do not create a NAT Gateway solely for screenshots. It can incur hourly and data-processing charges.

item.title: 5.3.1. Collect CPU, RAM, and Disk Metrics
item.description:
5.3.1. Collect CPU, RAM, and Disk Metrics

Objective

Publish EC2 CPU, memory, and disk utilization metrics to CloudWatch for monitoring and alert evaluation.

Steps

  1. Open CloudWatch → Metrics → All metrics and find AWS/EC2 → CPUUtilization for the target InstanceId. CPU is an EC2 standard metric.

  1. For memory and disk, install and configure Amazon CloudWatch Agent on Ubuntu. The instance role must permit metric publishing, for example through suitable CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy permissions.

item.title: 5.4.1. Create NetworkDevices and NetworkAlerts Tables
item.description:
5.4.1. Create NetworkDevices and NetworkAlerts Tables

Objective

Design NoSQL storage for the device inventory and alert history. Reuse existing tables instead of creating duplicates.

Create or verify tables

  1. Open DynamoDB → Tables in us-east-1.
  2. Create or verify NetworkDevices with String partition key deviceId and On-demand capacity.
  1. Create or verify NetworkAlerts with String partition key eventId and On-demand capacity.
  1. A sort key is not needed for the current single-key design. Add indexes only after identifying a real query requirement.

Example device record

{
 "deviceId": "TEST-SW01",
 "deviceName": "Demo Switch",
 "deviceType": "Switch",
 "ipAddress": "10.0.0.10",
 "status": "Online"
}

For EC2, optional fields include instanceId, region, monitoringSource, and vpcId. Do not enter InstanceId in the IP field: the two fields identify different things.

item.title: 5.5.1. Create a Cognito User Pool and Web Client
item.description:
5.5.1. Create a Cognito User Pool and Web Client

Objective

Create a managed sign-in flow for NetMon administrators with Amazon Cognito rather than allowing unauthenticated browser access to the APIs.

Steps

  1. Open Amazon Cognito → User pools. Create a pool or select the existing one in us-east-1.
  1. Create an App client for a Single-page application (SPA) and name it netmon-web-client.

  1. Use email as the sign-in identifier, and keep self-registration disabled if only approved team members should have accounts.

item.title: 5.6.1. Test from the UI to CloudWatch/DynamoDB
item.description:
5.6.1. Test from the UI to CloudWatch/DynamoDB

Objective

Run reproducible tests showing that the team’s infrastructure, backend, and monitoring/interface components work together as one workflow.

Suggested test cases

ID Test action Expected result
T01 Request GET /devices without JWT 401 Unauthorized
T02 Sign in with Cognito and PKCE Obtain a valid Access Token
T03 GET /devices with read scope Receive the device list
T04 POST /devices with TEST-SW01 Record created in NetworkDevices
T05 GET/PUT /devices/{id} Read and update the test device
T06 DELETE /devices/{id} Delete only the test device
T07 GET /alerts Read events in NetworkAlerts
T08 PUT /alerts/{id} Change handlingStatus to Acknowledged or Resolved
T09 GET /metrics Get real CloudWatch CPU data when available
T10 Change a demo alarm state in a controlled test Verify SNS and stored alert history

Evidence

Capture Cognito Users (hide email addresses for public use), JWT routes, Lambda Test, DynamoDB Scan, CloudWatch Alarms, EventBridge rule, redacted SNS email, and API Test results. Label evidence screenshots T01, T02, etc.

item.title: 5.1.2. IAM Setup and Team Roles
item.description:
5.1.2. IAM Setup and Team Roles

Objective

Assign project responsibilities and configure IAM so that each teammate can work without sharing credentials.

Team responsibilities

Member Responsibility
Tung Duong VPC, public/private subnets, route tables, Internet Gateway, Security Groups, EC2
Xuan Duc Lambda, DynamoDB, API Gateway, device CRUD, and alert APIs
Manh Quan CloudWatch, SNS, interface, and testing

Steps

  1. Open IAM → Users. Create separate IAM users, or use AWS IAM Identity Center if it is available.

item.title: 5.2.2. Launch an Ubuntu EC2 Instance
item.description:
5.2.2. Launch an Ubuntu EC2 Instance

Objective

Launch an Ubuntu server for CloudWatch monitoring tests while reducing unauthorized-access risks.

Steps

  1. Open EC2 → Instances → Launch instances.

  2. Set the instance name to netmon-ec2-server, matching the lab naming convention.

  3. Choose Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS and an instance type appropriate to the available budget and usage limits.

  4. In Network settings, select the intended VPC and public subnet and review public IP assignment.

item.title: 5.3.2. Create CloudWatch Alarms and SNS Email
item.description:
5.3.2. Create CloudWatch Alarms and SNS Email

Objective

Create CPU, memory, and disk alarms and use SNS to send notifications when configured thresholds are exceeded.

Create an SNS Topic

  1. Go to Amazon SNS → Topics → Create topic, select Standard, and name it netmon-alerts.

  2. Open the topic and choose Create subscription. Select Email and provide the recipient address.

  3. Open the AWS SNS confirmation message and select Confirm subscription. A Pending confirmation subscription cannot receive notifications.

item.title: 5.4.2. Build the netmon-api Python Lambda
item.description:
5.4.2. Build the netmon-api Python Lambda

Objective

Use a single Python Lambda named netmon-api to serve eight HTTP operations based on the request method and path, avoiding unnecessary duplicate functions for the class project.

Steps

  1. Open Lambda → Functions → Create function → Author from scratch. Name the function netmon-api and select a supported Python runtime.
  1. Attach an execution role with access to both DynamoDB tables, cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics, and CloudWatch Logs. Prefer resource-scoped DynamoDB permissions.

  1. In code, read the method from event.requestContext.http.method and the URL from event.rawPath for HTTP API payload format 2.0.

item.title: 5.5.2. Create a JWT Authorizer and OAuth Scopes
item.description:
5.5.2. Create a JWT Authorizer and OAuth Scopes

Objective

Require a valid access token and an appropriate scope before API Gateway allows NetMon read or write operations.

Resource server and OAuth scopes

  1. Open Cognito → User pool → Applications → Resource servers → Create resource server.
  2. Set Name NetMon API, Identifier netmon-api, and add custom scopes read and write.
  3. Under App clients → netmon-web-client → Login pages → Edit, allow netmon-api/read, netmon-api/write, and the necessary OpenID scopes (such as openid and email). Save changes.

JWT Authorizer

  1. Open API Gateway → netmon-management-api → Authorization → Manage authorizers → Create.

item.title: 5.6.2. Review Costs and Preserve Evidence
item.description:
5.6.2. Review Costs and Preserve Evidence

Objective

Finish a lab session without avoidable charges while preserving the resources needed for the team’s final demonstration.

Cost checklist

  1. Open Billing → Cost Explorer / Bills and record actual spending by service and Region.
  2. Review AWS Budgets and recipient email addresses, especially around the 25%, 50%, and 100% thresholds of the group’s USD 20/month plan.

  1. Check EC2 → Instances and consider Stop when monitoring is not required. EBS and some attached resources can still incur costs.

item.title: 5.1.3. AWS Budgets and Cost Controls
item.description:
5.1.3. AWS Budgets and Cost Controls

Goal

Set up AWS cost monitoring for the lab. A USD 20 budget is an alert threshold—not actual spending or a hard spending cap.

Console steps

  1. Open Billing and Cost Management → Budgets → Create budget; choose Cost budget.
  2. Choose Monthly, enter USD 20, and name the budget netmon-monthly-budget or another meaningful name.
  1. Configure percentage-based email alerts. During the lab, the team adjusted one alert threshold to 25%; other useful thresholds are 50% and 100%.
  1. Enter the alert recipient email and complete any email verification required.
  2. Review actual charges under Cost Explorer or Bills, particularly EC2, EBS, CloudWatch, DynamoDB, and any networking resources.

Verification

  • Confirm that the budget is listed and recipients are correct.
  • Check the currency, monthly period, and warning thresholds.
  • Redact email addresses before publishing cost-console screenshots.

Note: EC2 uptime, EBS storage, public IPv4, NAT Gateway (if used), and CloudWatch usage may incur charges. Do not assume the entire system is free.

item.title: 5.2.3. Security Groups, IAM Roles, and Safe Access
item.description:
5.2.3. Security Groups, IAM Roles, and Safe Access

Goal

Protect netmon-ec2-server and enable monitoring without exposing management ports to the entire Internet.

Console steps

  1. Open EC2 → Instances, select netmon-ec2-server, and open Security.
  2. Inspect the attached Security Group → Inbound rules. Do not expose TCP/22 to 0.0.0.0/0 without a justified, reviewed need.

  1. If using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, verify the SSM Agent, IAM instance profile, and required network connectivity; otherwise use another restricted administration path.

item.title: 5.3.3. Route Alarm Changes with EventBridge
item.description:
5.3.3. Route Alarm Changes with EventBridge

Objective

When a CloudWatch Alarm changes state, EventBridge invokes a Lambda function that stores alert history in DynamoDB for time tracking and incident handling.

Steps

  1. Ensure that the NetworkAlerts table exists with String partition key eventId.

  2. Create the Python Lambda netmon-save-alert and give its execution role dynamodb:PutItem on the NetworkAlerts table and CloudWatch Logs permissions.

  3. Open Amazon EventBridge → Event buses → default → Rules → Create rule. Name it netmon-alarm-state-rule on the default event bus.

item.title: 5.4.3. Build an HTTP API with Eight Routes
item.description:
5.4.3. Build an HTTP API with Eight Routes

Objective

Create an HTTP API for NetMon management actions and integrate all routes with netmon-api Lambda.

AWS Console steps

  1. Open API Gateway → APIs → Create API → HTTP API. The group’s API is called netmon-management-api.
  2. Create or verify these routes:
Route Purpose
GET /devices List devices
POST /devices Create device
GET /devices/{id} Get device details
PUT /devices/{id} Update device
DELETE /devices/{id} Delete device
GET /alerts List alerts
PUT /alerts/{id} Update alert handling status
GET /metrics Retrieve CPU metrics (current Lambda behavior)
  1. Under Develop → Integrations, select the netmon-api Lambda function in us-east-1, payload format 2.0, and attach it to all eight routes.
  1. Under Develop → CORS, set allowed origin http://localhost:5500, methods GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS, and headers authorization and content-type. Credentials are not required when sending JWTs in the Authorization header.
  1. Under Deploy → Stages → $default, confirm Automatic deployment = Enabled. If disabled, deploy manually.

Initial test

Once routes have JWT authorization, requesting GET /devices without an Authorization header should return 401 Unauthorized. This verifies the authorization layer, not the full Lambda integration. Test with a valid access token to confirm the backend.

item.title: 5.5.3. Build a VS Code Test Page
item.description:
5.5.3. Build a VS Code Test Page

Objective

Use an HTML/CSS/JavaScript test interface in VS Code to sign in with Cognito, call the API, and verify real data without waiting for the final UI maintained by Manh Quan.

Preparation

  1. Open the prepared NetMon-API-Test project in VS Code, or use a frontend with an equivalent PKCE implementation.
  2. Run a local server from the directory containing index.html:
python -m http.server 5500
  1. Open http://localhost:5500/ and make sure the page loads before starting Cognito sign-in.
  1. Enter the correct Cognito domain, App Client ID, and API Gateway Invoke URL. Never enter AWS Secret Keys or a Cognito client secret into browser code.
  2. Use the frontend’s sign-in button. After Cognito redirects to /?code=..., JavaScript completes the PKCE code exchange and receives an Access Token.
  3. Test GET /devices and GET /alerts. If they succeed, create a TEST-SW01 device, update its details, read it, and delete only that test record.

Troubleshooting

Symptom What to check
ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED No local server is listening on localhost:5500
401 Unauthorized Missing, invalid, or expired token
403 Forbidden Access Token lacks the required route scope
CORS blocked Incorrect allowed origin or headers in API Gateway
500 Lambda, DynamoDB, IAM, or CloudWatch Logs

Never publish a live ?code= URL or real tokens. Before integrating the final UI, check that all eight routes return expected responses from the backend.

item.title: 5.6.3. Clean Up CloudWatch, SNS, and EventBridge
item.description:
5.6.3. Clean Up CloudWatch, SNS, and EventBridge

When to do this

Only clean up after the demo is complete and all evidence has been backed up. Do not delete alarms, SNS topics, or EventBridge rules if alerting is still required.

Cleanup steps

  1. Open CloudWatch → Alarms and capture the settings/history of netmon-cpu-high-80, netmon-ram-high-80, and netmon-disk-high-85.

  1. Delete alarms individually only after their monitoring purpose has ended. This stops alarm evaluation; it does not delete EC2.

item.title: 5.3.4. Store Alert History with Lambda and DynamoDB
item.description:
5.3.4. Store Alert History with Lambda and DynamoDB

Goal

Store CloudWatch Alarm State Change events in NetworkAlerts, tracking occurrence time and whether the incident has been handled.

Console steps

  1. Open DynamoDB → Tables and verify NetworkAlerts, with String partition key eventId.
  2. Open Lambda → Functions → netmon-save-alert. Deploy code that parses event.detail.alarmName, event.detail.state.value, event.id, and the event timestamp.

  1. Under Configuration → Permissions, grant the execution role dynamodb:PutItem to the NetworkAlerts table ARN, plus CloudWatch Logs permissions.

item.title: 5.4.4. Test CRUD and Data Queries
item.description:
5.4.4. Test CRUD and Data Queries

Goal

Validate CRUD operations on NetworkDevices using a dedicated test item, without changing the real EC2/device records used for the project.

Sample test record

Use a deviceId beginning with TEST-, for example:

{
 "deviceId": "TEST-SW01",
 "deviceName": "Switch test NetMon",
 "deviceType": "Switch",
 "ipAddress": "10.0.0.250",
 "status": "Online"
}

CRUD scenario

  1. POST /devices: create TEST-SW01 and verify it exists in DynamoDB.
  2. GET /devices: list devices and locate the test item.

  1. GET /devices/TEST-SW01: verify device details.

item.title: 5.5.4. Sign In with PKCE and Call Protected APIs
item.description:
5.5.4. Sign In with PKCE and Call Protected APIs

Goal

Connect an HTML/JavaScript NetMon test page to Cognito and obtain an Access Token through Authorization Code + PKCE.

Configuration

  1. In Cognito → App clients → netmon-web-client, verify SPA type and Authorization code grant.
  2. Use the exact callback http://localhost:5500/ and scopes openid email netmon-api/read netmon-api/write; never include a client secret in browser code.

  1. Start the web server first, e.g. python -m http.server 5500, and ensure http://localhost:5500/ loads.

item.title: 5.6.4. Clean Up Lambda, DynamoDB, and API Gateway
item.description:
5.6.4. Clean Up Lambda, DynamoDB, and API Gateway

Before removing resources

Finish the demo and back up relevant screenshots, logs, API configuration, and test data. Deleting a DynamoDB table may irreversibly remove data.

Steps

  1. DynamoDB: Export or back up NetworkDevices and NetworkAlerts before deletion. Do not remove them while the frontend is still being tested.
  1. API Gateway: Document the eight Routes, Authorizer, CORS, Stage, and Integration for netmon-management-api, then delete it only when no frontend depends on it.
  1. AWS Lambda: Review event targets and triggers before deleting netmon-api or netmon-save-alert.

  1. IAM roles: Remove only roles dedicated to services that have been retired; preserve any role shared with EC2 or other applications.

item.title: 5.6.5. Clean Up Cognito and Networking Resources
item.description:
5.6.5. Clean Up Cognito and Networking Resources

Goal

Revoke access after the project and remove infrastructure that may continue generating charges.

Cleanup steps

  1. Amazon Cognito: Confirm the User Pool used by netmon-web-client. An application user in Cognito is different from an IAM user who accesses AWS Console.

  1. When testing is complete, back up relevant configuration and remove the App Client, Resource Server, and User Pool as appropriate. Deleting the pool prevents NetMon users from signing in.
